items.title: Two Scattered Spider Hackers Get 5.5 Years Each for £29 Million TfL Hack
items.description: Owen Flowers, 18, and Thalha Jubair, 20, were each sentenced to five and a half years at Woolwich Crown Court on Thursday, 16 July 2026, for the 2024 hack of Transport for London. The attack left 148 TfL systems inoperable and forced all 27,000 of the transport authority's employees into an office to get their passwords reset in person. items.title: Linus Torvalds Told Kernel Developers that Linux is Not Against AI projects
items.description: Linux creator Linus Torvalds has told kernel developers that the Linux project is not anti-AI, arguing that artificial intelligence and large language models should be judged on whether they provide practical technical value. He emphasized that developers will not be forced to use AI tools, but opposition should not prevent others from using them responsibly. […] The post Linus Torvalds Told…

items.title: ThreatsDay: Game Cheat Spyware, 24-Hour Ransomware, Chrome Sync Stalking + 12 More Stories
items.description: A lot of this week’s trouble starts with something that looks close enough. A familiar repo. A useful installer. A harmless sync setting. Then the handoff goes bad, the box starts talking to someone else, and the damage moves faster than the explanation. Old bugs are back, weak defaults are earning their keep, and some attack paths are so plain they barely feel like research. Here’s the mess.

items.title: n8n Token Exchange Flaw Could Let Attackers Log In as Users From Another Issuer
items.description: n8n, the workflow automation platform, handed out the wrong accounts at login.
